question: Would a PHOSITA have had a reason to modify an endovascular CSF-drug-delivery platform to retain the therapeutic agent while still permitting clinically adequate CSF drainage?

motivation.evidence: The PROBLEM (rapid CSF clearance reducing drug exposure) is recognized in the literature. The SOLUTION (selective retention while draining) is NOT taught in any of 15+ charted patents.
motivation.status: NO MOTIVATION FOUND — the problem is known but the solution (retention while maintaining drainage) is not taught. A PHOSITA seeing the problem would not necessarily think of selective retention as the solution.
motivation.evidence_basis: 0/15 patents teach retention + drainage combination. PatSnap search returned 0 additional results.

expected_success.evidence: A PHOSITA would expect that a retention element in a drainage path would REDUCE drainage (obstruction risk). The 288% exposure improvement with FULL drainage preservation is unexpected.
expected_success.status: UNEXPECTED — the conventional expectation is that retention and drainage are antagonistic. The model shows they are compatible (100% drainage preserved across 200 parameter combinations).

compatible_mechanisms.evidence: Selective retention (size-based membrane) and CSF drainage (pressure-driven flow) operate on different physical principles — retention is molecular-size-selective, drainage is bulk flow.
compatible_mechanisms.status: COMPATIBLE — but a PHOSITA would not necessarily recognize this without the model.

teaching_away.evidence: The rapid CSF turnover (~7h half-time) and high drainage rate (1.4 mL/min) may teach AWAY from attempting drug residence in the shunt, as the conventional wisdom is that CSF drugs are quickly cleared.
teaching_away.status: PARTIAL TEACHING AWAY — the high drainage rate suggests retention would be difficult.

unexpected_technical_result.evidence: 288% improvement (retention alone) is much larger than a PHOSITA would predict. The architecture beats 3x dose escalation (200%). Controlled release alone produces only 2%.
unexpected_technical_result.status: YES — unexpected magnitude. But this is evidence ONLY AFTER the prior-art combination has been established. The 288% cannot substitute for motivation analysis.
unexpected_technical_result.critical_rule: The 288% effect can be evidence of unexpected results ONLY AFTER the prior-art combination has been established — not as a substitute for motivation analysis.

conclusion.rationale: No motivation found (0/15 patents teach the combination). Expected success is unexpected (retention + drainage are conventionally antagonistic). Teaching away (high CSF turnover). Unexpected magnitude (288%). Patent counsel opinion required.
